newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DEL PIERO'S TWO GOALS GIVE JUVENTUS FIVE-POINT LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEL PIERO'S TWO GOALS GIVE JUVENTUS FIVE-POINT LEAD.

text.p: Alessandro Del Piero scored two goals for the second time in a week as Juventus recovered from 2-0 down to beat Verona 3-2 on Sunday and take a five-point lead in Italy's serie A.

Juventus' s title ambitions were helped by Vicenza's 1-1 draw with Parma in a late kickoff and Internazionale's 4-3 defeat by Sampdoria, who came from 3-1 down to win with a goal from Roberto Mancini two minutes from time.
Juventus have 28 points from 13 matches, five clear of Vicenza and seven ahead of Inter who trail Milan and Bologna on goal difference.
Mancini's winner was the perfect answer to Inter coach Roy Hodgson's famous question when his president Massimo Moratti tried to buy the player earlier this season.

"Mancini who?" said Hodgson. At the San Siro the most prolific striker currently playing serie A soccer reminded the English coach of his credentials, completing a dramatic Sampdoria comeback with his 132nd career goal.
In a thrilling match, Sampdoria made the perfect start with a seventh minute goal from Vincenzo Montella.
Inter drew level through Marco Branca in the 13th, took the lead with a close range shot from Nicola Berti in the 43rd and looked to have sealed victory with Branca's second straight after the break.
At this stage Mancini, whose move to Inter was vetoed by his club, took over.

In the 56th minute he set up Montella's second with a pinpoint cross, then, after Marco Franceschetti had levelled the scores in the 85th minute, Sampdoria's captain delivered the coup de grace from close-range.
After the match angry fans hurled stones that shattered windows in the VIP lounge at the San Siro. "I understand their anger," said Hogdson, "it was a very, very bad result for us."
Hodgson's mood hardly improved as news filtered through of Juve's comeback at the Stadio delle Alpi.
The European champions were given a shock when Felippo Maniero finished off swift Verona counter-attacks in clinical fashion in the 25th and 44th minutes.
Without injured striker Alen Boksic, it was left to defender Sergio Porrini to pull Juve back into the game with an untidy goal just before halftime.

After the break Del Piero levelled the scores when he calmly slotted home a penalty. Then in the 72nd minute the same player unleashed a vicious, curling shot from 20 metres to brilliantly clinch Juve's fourth successive league win.
At the Stadio Menti, Vicenza shrugged off the first half dismissal of Gilberto D'Ignazo to take the lead through Giampiero Maini's 50th minute header.
But the strain of playing with 10 men eventually told and Antonio Benarrivo claimed a 72nd equaliser for Carlo Ancelotti's struggling Parma.

AC Milan climbed to third on 21 points after their second successive league victory under Arrigo Sacchi -- courtesy of three goals from Italy's Demetrio Albertini, including two from the penalty spot, at bottom-of-the-table Reggiana.
After the match Sacchi played down reports that Roberto Baggio was about to leave Milan following a row with his coach.
"In 23 years as a coach I have never raised my voice with a player," said Sacchi. "My friendship for Roberto remains the same."
At the San Siro Inter fans made their feelings plain about Baggio's reported interest in a transfer to their club. "No thanks," read one banner.
